contributions.statement: Reject agent-generated JUnit tests that wrap the call under test in a catch-all try/catch; swallowed exceptions were the single largest reason generated tests missed a breaking change in Java/Maven upgrades.
contributions.evidence: §VI-A/§VI-C manual inspection of 80 of 455 non-detecting tests that loaded the broken class: 32/80 swallowed exceptions in catch blocks, 11/80 used non-triggering inputs.

contributions.statement: Do not count LLM-generated client-usage tests on dependency bumps as behavioural contract coverage: 95% of what they catch is crash-type (missing class/method) breakage that a static API diff such as japicmp already finds, and only 0.7% of detecting tests use value assertions.
contributions.evidence: §V-C Table VI: 95.1% of detections are runtime errors; 25 detecting tests (0.7%) use value-based assertions. Best config detects 27/89 (Table V), all on instances the client suite already caught (audit).

reason: Java-native negative result with a mechanism (exception swallowing, no value assertions) that yields a concrete lint rule for agent-written tests. The headline 30% detection rate adds nothing over existing client suites.
